meta.title: AI Chip Packaging Stack
meta.lede: A signal leaving the GPU die crosses four carriers before it reaches the motherboard. Each one is built from a different material set, and each one has a different supply base. Click any layer to see what it is made of, who makes it, and where it binds.

p: The numbering is not a taxonomy. It is the order the signal actually travels. Moving outward from the die, pad pitch widens by roughly an order of magnitude at every step, and the material set changes with it. 01 is innermost, 04 is the board.

A working map of the AI chip packaging supply chain, built bottom-up from company filings and sell-side research on the Taiwan and Japan supply base. The cost model on the PCB layer is my own derivation.

Impact analysis. Each node carries concentration, sole-source status and qualification lead time, so a capacity or pricing event can be traced through to how many racks it gates and how long a substitution would take.

layers.name: Die & HBM
layers.en: LOGIC DIE AND HIGH BANDWIDTH MEMORY

spec.v: Logic die and high bandwidth memory
Innermost layer, where the signal starts
Compute itself, plus memory sitting right next to it
Logic operations and data staging
Silicon wafer. HBM is a vertical stack of DRAM dies joined by through-silicon vias

layers.note: HBM is the only thing on this map that sits in layer 01 and layer 02 at the same time. It needs a leading-edge DRAM process to make the dies and advanced packaging to stack twelve of them, so its supply behaves unlike the rest of memory. Neither gate opening is enough on its own. Micron has put a number on that with its three-to-one input ratio, meaning HBM3E consumes roughly three times the wafer of DDR5 for the same capacity, and has said the ratio rises in later generations. Add 2026 supply already sold out against a stated ability to meet only half to two-thirds of customer demand, and the gap is not something capex alone closes.
layers.note_basis: 富邦整理的美光 2026 年 10 月法說

layers.name: Advanced packaging

spec.v: Advanced packaging, 2.5D integration
Between the die and the substrate
Puts the GPU die and several HBM stacks on one common base
Very short reach, very high bandwidth die-to-die interconnect
Silicon interposer or redistribution layer, through-silicon vias, microbumps, underfill, molding compound

layers.note: This is the layer the industry agrees has been tightest. What binds here is not process yield the way it would be in a fab. It is physical interposer capacity and the time it takes to stand up more of it.
layers.note_basis: 初始骨架，尚未綁定出處

layers.name: IC substrate

spec.v: IC substrate, ABF substrate at the high end
Between the package and the board
Fans the fine package pitch out to something the board can actually attach to
Signal fan-out, mechanical support, part of the thermal path
ABF build-up film carries no glass. The core layer is a glass-reinforced laminate. Plus copper foil, laser-drilled vias and solder balls

layers.note: Substrate pricing moves on the same line as PCB. The core of an ABF substrate is itself a laminate, Kinsus is qualifying a T-glass plus E-glass build, and Elite Material has started shipping core material into substrates. So when glass fabric and copper foil tighten, substrates tighten with them. Unimicron and Ibiden capacity is absorbed by AI GPUs and ASICs, which is why the next-generation AMD server CPU substrate went to Nan Ya PCB.
layers.note_basis: 核心層材料見台光電與景碩速報，產能排擠見南電 10 月速報，均為富邦

layers.name: PCB motherboard

spec.v: Printed circuit board
Outermost carrier
Carries the modules, distributes power, routes signal off-board
Signal transmission and power delivery
Copper clad laminate, pressed from copper foil, resin and glass fabric, bonded layer to layer with prepreg

layers.note: The tightest input this year is not an exotic one. It is ordinary E-glass fabric, up more than 80% in the first half, which has held laminate makers at around 70-75% utilisation with order books they cannot fill. High-end copper foil tells the same story, with HVLP4 demand well above what the Japanese incumbents plus Co-Tech can put out. Look one step further up and the real gate is equipment. High-end looms are quoting into 2030 and treaters run 18 to 24 months, so how fast this layer expands is decided by the machine builders.
layers.note_basis: E-glass 漲幅八成以上見大和與高盛，稼動率 70 到 75% 見凱基、統一、大和，織布機交期見富邦富喬速報，上膠機交期見統一，HVLP4 缺口見未具名銅箔報告

die.name: TSMC
die.capacity_note: Customer N2 utilisation tracking to 50% in 2Q26, 80% in 3Q26 and 100% in 4Q26, with N2 and N3 capacity up roughly 70% and 25% year on year

die.name: Micron
die.role: HBM and DRAM. 2026 supply fully sold out, with the company stating it can meet only half to two-thirds of customer demand
die.capacity_note: FQ3 FY26 revenue around $42bn at over 81% gross margin, FQ4 guided near $50bn. $22bn of customer prepayments received and capex raised from $20bn to over $25bn. HBM4 revenue has passed $1bn and is ramping around twice as fast as HBM3E. 26 long-term agreements signed covering more than 35% of revenue to 2030, with more than 75% of 2027 output already committed. Singapore HBM advanced packaging starts in early 2027 and the Taiwan site ships mid-2027. Third of the three HBM suppliers by share

die.name: Advanced Echem Materials
die.role: Sole supplier of a rinse surface modifier used by foundry customers on every node below 40nm
die.capacity_note: Kaohsiung phase one full by 1H27, phase two in volume mid-2027. Front-end semiconductor materials take three to five years from development through qualification

die.name: Hanwha Semitech
die.role: SK hynix bonder partner. A commercial hybrid bonding launch depends on this class of equipment

die.name: BE Semiconductor
die.role: The main hybrid bonding equipment supplier, which is what stacking moves to after HBM4E

die.name: ASMPT
die.role: Thermocompression bonders, the tools behind today's mainstream HBM stacking

die.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
die.role: One of the two dominant wafer makers

die.name: SUMCO
die.role: One of the two dominant wafer makers

die.name: Tokyo Electron
die.role: Coat and develop, etch, deposition and thermal, so it spans several steps

die.name: ASML
die.role: The only source of EUV scanners anywhere, so every step down in linewidth runs through one company

die.name: Lam Research
die.role: Etch and deposition. Deep via etch is what makes TSVs possible

die.name: Applied Materials
die.role: The largest supplier of thin film deposition and metal wiring tools

die.name: Advantest
die.role: A main supplier of memory and SoC testers

die.name: ChipMOS
die.role: Memory test and assembly. Wafer sort is the gate that finds the good dies before stacking

pkg.name: Jentech Precision
pkg.role: Largest maker of package-level thermal hardware. GPU lids, heat spreaders and stiffener rings. Rubin content runs three to four times B300
pkg.capacity_note: One of four qualified suppliers for VR200 microchannel cold plates, alongside AVC, Cooler Master and Delta

pkg.name: All Ring Tech
pkg.role: Dispensing and inspection equipment for CoWoS, and the dispensing supplier for TSMC SoIC wafer-on-wafer
pkg.capacity_note: CoWoS and FoCoS equipment runs around 87% of 2026 revenue

pkg.name: Intel
pkg.role: The other 2.5D route besides CoWoS. The Google and MediaTek ASIC is reported to use EMIB-T
pkg.capacity_note: Advanced packaging capacity reported to double in each of 2027 and 2028

pkg.name: Powertech Technology
pkg.role: FOPLP entering pilot qualification, volume targeted for mid-2027, also developing HBM packaging for customers

pkg.name: AP Memory
pkg.role: Integrated passive device silicon capacitors, built at PSMC, working to qualify into EMIB and CoWoS packages
pkg.capacity_note: IPD targeted at more than 35% of revenue next year

sub.name: Ajinomoto
sub.role: Build-up film. Essentially no qualified alternative

sub.name: Ibiden
sub.role: ABF substrate. Capacity absorbed by AI GPUs and ASICs while also carrying the Intel EMIB ramp

sub.name: Unimicron
sub.role: ABF and BT substrate. Yangmei and Luzhu both full, with customers prepaying to reserve capacity
sub.capacity_note: Luzhu phase three starts 2H26, phase two volume in 2027, Yangmei fab two in 2028. Resonac and MGC price increases have been passed through. General-purpose servers account for an estimated 25-30% of ABF demand and AI servers 30-35%

sub.name: Nan Ya PCB
sub.role: ABF and BT substrate. Picks up AMD Venice from 1Q27 as Ibiden and Unimicron capacity is taken by AI
sub.capacity_note: 2Q26 ABF utilisation 80-85%, BT full. Estimated to take more than half of Venice. ABF capacity up 5-10% in each of FY27 and FY28, mostly through debottlenecking. NT$46.8bn capex for a large-format CoPoS substrate fab, with the Chiayi site in volume around FY29

sub.name: Kinsus Interconnect
sub.role: ABF substrate, expanding on the Nvidia Vera CPU ramp, estimated to take more than half of Vera in 2027
sub.capacity_note: ABF capacity 40m units per month in FY26, 50m from 2Q27, 65m in FY28 and 80m in FY29. Qualifying a T-glass plus E-glass build. With T-glass, copper foil and ABF film all rising, quarterly price increases of 5-10% are expected

pcb.name: Gold Circuit Electronics
pcb.role: High layer count boards for servers and switches. Capacity up more than 25% since May and still short of demand
pcb.capacity_note: Combined capacity measured at NT$9.4bn of output value, against NT$7.5bn in May. AI-related was 40-50% of 2Q26. ASIC customers may move from HLC to a mixed HDI plus HLC build

pcb.name: Zhen Ding Technology
pcb.role: Built on flex, now shifting weight toward IC substrate and server boards, with building 13 under construction and 16 in planning
pcb.capacity_note: New capacity phased in from 2026 to 2030, with the company stating that expansion is contracted to customers. IC substrate estimated at 12% of revenue in 2027

pcb.name: ITEQ
pcb.role: The volume laminate supplier for general-purpose servers, concentrated on E-glass with M6 to M7 resin systems, holding more than 60% of the AMD platform
pcb.share_scope: 範圍不同的兩個估計並存，高盛估 2024 年全球伺服器 CCL 市佔 15 到 20%，統一估 AMD 平台逾六成、Intel 平台三到四成，所以不填單一數字
pcb.capacity_note: Monthly capacity around 5.4m sheets in 2025, on a path to roughly 5.7m, 6.3m, 8.3m and 9.2m sheets through 2029. The 2.85m sheets added at Wuxi are dedicated to M7 and above. Utilisation held at 70-75% by E-glass supply. Industry treater lead times run 18 to 24 months. 4Q26 pricing up a further 15-20%, with fabric suppliers releasing small volumes that should lift utilisation toward 80%

pcb.name: Elite Material
pcb.role: The high-end laminate leader. M9 moving from single digit to double digit share of mix, and now shipping core material into ABF substrates
pcb.capacity_note: 3Q26 revenue NT$60.9bn. 4Q26 pricing up 5-10% on average, with the steeper increases at M6 and below. High-end capacity expected to add 3.15m sheets per month in 2027. Substrate material was historically BT-based and under 1% of revenue

pcb.name: Taiwan Union Technology
pcb.role: High-end laminate. M7 and above is 36% of mix, utilisation full, M9 in final qualification
pcb.capacity_note: 2.6m sheets per month exiting 2Q26, adding 600k each at Changshu and Thailand, reaching 3.8m by the end of 2027

pcb.name: Fu Chiao (1815)
pcb.role: Integrated from yarn through fabric. Low DK1, Low DK2 and Low CTE all in production, with Taiwan and Dongguan weaving full
pcb.capacity_note: Two furnaces plus four electric furnaces and 920 looms. Thailand phase one of 400 looms starts in 3Q27 with initial output already reserved by customers, expanding to 500 in 2028. Toyota automatic looms for high-end fabric are quoting delivery into 2030. July pricing up 30% on E-glass and 15% on Low DK2

pcb.name: Mitsui Kinzoku
pcb.role: The main Japanese HVLP supplier. Most of the installed base is still first generation, and usable capacity shrinks with every generation step
pcb.capacity_note: Around 620 t per month, predominantly HVLP1. Converted entirely to HVLP4 that same line yields only 320 t. Total capacity rises to 840 t after September 2026, which is still only 400-430 t if all of it runs HVLP4

pcb.name: Furukawa Electric
pcb.role: One of the two main HVLP4 sources, and where Elite Material takes most of its HVLP4
pcb.capacity_note: Mitsui and Furukawa combined ran roughly 350 t per month of HVLP4 in 2025, expanding to 450-550 t by the end of 2026, against 2026 demand of about 1,200 t per month

pcb.name: Co-Tech Development
pcb.role: The Taiwanese HVLP foil maker, selling to Elite Material, Taiwan Union and ITEQ, ramping HVLP4 to close the Japanese shortfall
pcb.capacity_note: 250 t per month across all foil, with 480 t of headroom at the third Yunlin plant. HVLP4 at 50-100 t per month, expected to reach 200-250 t during 2026. Foil equipment lead times run six months or more and new capacity takes 18 to 24 months to come online

models.name: AI high-end PCB cost breakdown
models.unit: 佔上一層成本的百分比

models.name: Demand amplification from a laminate grade step
models.crucial_note: Layer count is set by the design and is effectively known. Yield and size are the only two variables that move with process maturity, so those are the two questions that decide where in the range a programme lands.

scenarios.label: base case
scenarios.note: Layer counts pair 12 to 24 and 16 to 32, not crosswise. Doubling layer count also doubles board thickness.

scenarios.label: GB300 largest board, upper bound
scenarios.note: 8.6 to 16.3× off a 16-layer base, 11.5 to 21.6× off a 12-layer base. This assumes three extremes land together, so it is a bound rather than a forecast and should be read separately from the base case.

downstream.note: 層數加倍在物理上就是疊更多層銅箔，所以 CCL 用量倍數大致帶動高階銅箔用量同倍數。成本佔比與用量倍數是兩件事，此處能接是因為層數因子本身就是銅箔張數

root.name: HBM stack
root.note: A stack is only good if every die in it is good. Twelve dies in series is where the hard part of this chain lives.

top.name: The dies in a stack
top.note: A stack holds two kinds of die. Twelve are DRAM, made on a memory process in the memory makers' own fabs. The thirteenth is the base die at the bottom, carrying the external interface and control logic. From HBM4 it moves off the memory process onto a foundry logic process, which opens an external link in what used to be a closed memory chain.

steps.name: Wafer manufacturing
steps.note: Crystal growth, slicing, lapping and polish. HBM starts on the same silicon as any other DRAM. What changes is everything after.

steps.name: Oxidation
steps.note: Growing a silicon dioxide layer for insulation and protection. Almost every later step builds on it.

steps.name: Photolithography
steps.note: Projecting the circuit pattern onto resist. Linewidth is decided here, and EUV scanners come from exactly one company, which makes this the cleanest single point of dependency in the whole semiconductor chain.

steps.name: Etching
steps.note: Removing what the resist does not protect. Through-silicon vias are cut by this class of process at aspect ratios far beyond ordinary structures, and it is part of why HBM takes longer in the fab.

steps.name: Deposition
steps.note: Building dielectric and metal layers one at a time. More layers means more passes through this step.

steps.name: Metal wiring
steps.note: Connecting the devices. HBM through-silicon vias have to be filled with copper, which is harder and slower than ordinary DRAM metallisation.

steps.name: Electric die sorting
steps.note: Testing on the wafer before dicing to find the good dies. This matters more for HBM than for anything else, because stacking a bad die scraps all twelve.

demand._comment: 需求推導用的機櫃規格。capacity 類數字取自 NVIDIA 官方規格頁，stacks_per_gpu 與 dies_per_stack 是由容量推導的參數不是官方揭露，confidence 標 3 並在 basis 寫明。改這裡的數字，頁面上的計算會跟著變。

racks.name: GB200 NVL72
racks.note: The first NVL72 rack. 192 GB per GPU works out to roughly 13.8 TB across the rack.
racks.basis: Capacity per GPU is public spec. Eight stacks per GPU and eight dies per stack are derived from capacity divided by the generation's per-stack size, not disclosed figures

racks.name: GB300 NVL72
racks.note: Physically each GPU sits next to 8 HBM3E stacks, 12 layers each at 3 GB a layer, which is 288 GB. That is what the memory maker actually ships. NVIDIA's spec page lists 279 GB, the capacity a user can address, and 279 times 72 is exactly the 20 TB it quotes for the rack. The missing 9 GB is not explained officially. Industry reading points to reserved capacity or a layer switched off for yield, neither confirmed. The cascade uses 288, because that 9 GB of silicon still got made.
racks.basis: 72 GPUs and 20 TB per rack come from NVIDIA's rack spec page. 288 GB per GPU comes from NVIDIA's enterprise reference architecture, which separately lists 2304 GB across an eight-GPU baseboard, and 2304 divided by eight is exactly 288. The 36 GB, 12-high, 24 Gb-per-die stack is Micron's own HBM3E product specification, confirmed by a TechInsights teardown of a physical B300 package. Neither company states stacks per GPU. Eight falls out of 288 divided by 36, so it is not an assumption but two companies' published figures reconciling.

racks.name: Vera Rubin NVL72
racks.note: Moves to HBM4, where the interface doubles from 1024 to 2048 bits. The GPU package is a dual-die design and the rack carries 20.7 TB, which divided by 72 is about 288 GB, so this generation shows none of the gap between physical and usable capacity that GB300 does. Micron has announced HBM4 in high volume production for Vera Rubin.
racks.basis: 288 GB per GPU and 20.7 TB per rack are public reporting. The 36 GB 12-high stack is from Micron's HBM4 volume production announcement. Eight stacks follows from 288 divided by 36. Micron is also sampling a 48 GB 16-high part, and a switch to that would change the stack count per GPU.

racks.name: Rubin Ultra NVL576
racks.note: NVL576 counts 576 compute dies at four dies per package, so there are 144 packages. Each package carries 1 TB of HBM4E. This generation is still moving, so treat the numbers as order of magnitude.
racks.basis: Forward-looking public reporting, not final. Stacks and dies per stack are derived, not disclosed
